## Independent review of PR #223 at 2fe41a2

**Verdict: BLOCKING (2 items).** The PR fixes what it pins and causes no regression against its base 7fff05c. But the #208 mechanism still gives a trusted wrong axis on two families of parts. Both already fail the same way on the base, so neither is new to this PR. Both are still the bug this PR claims to fix with `Fixes #208`.

Probes: about 230 fixtures, run in a throwaway worktree at 2fe41a2 and again at 7fff05c (both through `fit_report`, twice each to check determinism). Nothing was committed.

### BLOCKING 1: split the pencil into three or more points on one line and the 50 % gate never fires

`borne_out` only checks the facets near ONE point, and only when they hold at least half of the inlier area. A prism whose side faces meet the axis at several points along it gets past both conditions. The coarseness gate then still counts the bearings of every facet, outliers included, so an off-centre boss supplies the bearings again. Each case below reads Z through the prism's centre line, `trusted = true`. The only turned feature is the boss, about its own centre:

| part (two triangles per rectangle, boss r5 h10, 72 segments, 1 band) | axis | aside |
|---|---|---|
| square bar 40x40x160, each side face split into 4 rectangles along its length (one solid), boss at (5, 0) on top | Z through (0, 0) | 0.011 |
| same, sides split into 3, length 120, boss at (5, 0) | Z through (0, 0) | 0.015 |
| same, boss at (10, 10) | Z through (0, 0) | 0.011 / 0.015 |
| stepped square block in one solid, steps 100/90/80 x 10, boss at (5, 0), (10, 0) or (20, 20) | Z through (0, 0) | 0.024-0.025 |
| 4 stacked 40 mm cube bodies, boss r3 or r5 at (5, 0), (10, 0) or (20, 20) | Z through (0, 0) | 0.004-0.012 |

With two steps instead of three (100x10 below 50x21), one step holds just over half the area, so it is refused. That shows the gate depends on how the pencil happens to be split.

Suggested fix: run the coarseness gate (`widest_skip`) on the **inliers** of the candidate axis, not on all facets. The module's own doc names the cause: the boss "lends its bearings to the coarseness gate". Facets set aside as outliers shouldn't be allowed to vouch for roundness. A true revolve's inliers carry every bearing on their own. A D-flat's flat line meets the axis, so it stays an inlier. Keyway walls and cross-hole walls are already outliers. Pin it with the square bar whose sides are split into 4, plus a boss at (5, 0), refused by name.

### BLOCKING 2: two single-band pencils at the same point lend each other bearings

A cross made of two crossed cylinders, Z r10 h100 (1 band) and Y r10 h60 (1 band), both centred on the origin. It reads **Y**, `trusted = true`, aside 0.056. The same happens with h60 x h60 (aside 0.073), with h60 x h100, and with Y in 5 bands. The Z cylinder's wall lines all pass through the origin, so they "meet" Y. The near set at that point holds both cylinders, and the Y cylinder's ring covers every bearing. So the near set passes as a whole, although half of it is a pencil with two bearings about Y. Turning about Y cuts the 100 mm Z rod down to a disc. With the Z rod in 5 bands it reads Z, so the answer depends on how the mesh was banded.

Suggested fix: inside `borne_out`, take out the facets that are each already a full ring about `ax` before running the pencil test. A cheaper option: require the near set's bearing coverage to hold per connected pencil, not for the union. Either way, pin the crossed-cylinder fixture as refused (or as Z, never Y).

### Re-run of the earlier probe set (head, then base)
- Plate 100x100x10 plus a boss at (10,0), (20,20), (2,0), (30,-10), (0,0) and (5,5), in 1 and 5 bands: all refused by name. A gain on (10,0).
- Cube 60 plus a boss in 5 positions and sizes, 1 and 5 bands: all refused ("equally").
- Hex bar h10/40/200, L-bracket, D-flats (r10 h100, depth 0.5-3, in 1/2/3/5 bands): same as base. Depth 1 or less reads Z exactly. Depth 1.5 or more is refused on both, so the "known cost" did not show up as a new refusal.
- Plate with a centred hole r20/r40 t10 and r45 t30: Z.
- Discs and short bars r50 h10/20 and r10 h5-h60, 1 and 5 bands: Z, exact. A tilted, off-origin single-band bar: exact.
- Ball with two parallel flats: Z. Ball with two perpendicular flats: now refused (base read Z with 5-7 % aside). Fine.
- Single-band shaft with a D-flat and a cross hole: depth 1 reads Z, depth 2 is refused. Base read X, trusted. Fixed.
- **Single-band shaft r10 h100 with a plain cross hole: base read X, trusted. Head reads Z.** A real fix the PR doesn't list.

### New probes
- T part: a plate 40x40x10 with a centred stem reads Z. An off-centre stem is refused. **A plate 100x100x10 with a centred r10 h60 stem is now refused (base: Z).** The plate's side faces hold just over half the inlier area. This fails closed, and a square plate isn't turned stock, so it isn't blocking. It is another place where the 50 % threshold flips the answer.
- Turned part with a large flange (r50 t10 plus a shaft r10 h100, bands 1/1, 5/1, 1/3 and 5/5, also tilted and offset, also with a square lug off-centre): exact axis every time, lug aside 0.7 %.
- Several separate turned bodies: two coaxial cylinders give Z. Two parallel ones, a big and a small one, and three in a row are all refused. Crossed cylinders: see BLOCKING 2.
- T-junction meshes: a cylinder in 1 band on one half and 3 bands on the other reads Z exactly. A T-junction plate or cube with a boss is refused.

### False refusals of real turned parts
None new. Cylinders in 1/2/3/5 bands, cones (r20->r5, r20->0 steep, r5->r30, in 1/2/5 bands), stepped and 3-step shafts (1/1, 5/5, 1/5, 2/2 bands), a cross-hole shaft and the punched r10x40 bar (#116-like) in 1/2/5 bands all read exactly. My keyway fixtures (w3 d1.5 up to w10 d4 on r10) are refused, but identically on base: the plain-fit drag of deep walls. Not this PR.

### Determinism, no panics, NaN
- Every probe gave bit-identical results on a second run.
- `pencil_point` sorts with `total_cmp`, `point_of` rejects a rank-deficient matrix through the eigenvalue floor, and every non-finite result is filtered.
- A mesh with NaN, infinite, zero-area and 1e300 facets mixed in reads Z. An all-NaN mesh and a single triangle are refused by name. Cylinders at 1e8 and 1e-6 scale read Z.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or indexing hazard in `axis_point.rs`.

Not approved, not merged.

Review blockers addressed in e883ae6 (plain push):

- **B1.** The coarseness gate (`widest_skip`) now reads only the facets whose normal lines meet the candidate axis, so an outlier boss supplies no bearings.
- **B2.** `borne_out` peels the inliers into pencils (lines through one point, then the next point among the rest; up to 12, each holding at least 5 % of the inlier area) and judges each pencil by itself. Its area-weighted trigonometric moments k = 1..4 about the axis must vanish. Weighted by pencil area, they may total at most 10 % of the inlier area. A pencil holding half the inliers must still pass the coarseness gate alone. A crossing rod's wall puts its share on two opposite bearings (k = 2) and a box on four (k = 4); a D-flat's lumped flat keeps the low moments nearly whole. I tried Kuiper's statistic first and dropped it: it reads two opposite lumps at half their share and could not separate a cross from a D-flat. Recorded in RECOMMENDED.md.

New pins (each fails on 2fe41a2):
- `a_square_bar_split_along_its_length_with_a_boss_is_refused_by_name`: 40x40x160 split into 4, 40x40x120 split into 3, boss at (5,0) and (10,10).
- `stepped_and_stacked_blocks_with_a_boss_are_refused_by_name`: 100/90/80 x 10 steps and 4 stacked 40 mm cubes, boss at (5,0), (10,0) and (20,20).
- `crossed_cylinders_never_read_the_cross_axis`: Z/Y h100/60, h60/60 and h60/100, plus Y in 5 bands. All are now refused.
- `a_single_band_shaft_with_a_shallow_flat_still_reads_its_axis`: guard, reads Z exactly.

Every earlier pin stays green, including the single-band bar.

Gate:
- motion lib: 143 passed.
- motion integration suites: multiaxis, multiaxis_avoid, multiaxis_rough, rotary, rotary_adaptive, rotary_links, rotary_offset and turning_* are green.
- app suites: drilling_cross*, lathe_* and turning* (21 binaries) are green.
- clippy on motion and app (all targets) is clean.

Known cost (fails closed): crossed rods of any proportion are refused, including a cross pin holding more than about 10 % of the inlier area. The plate 100x100x10 with a centred stem stays refused.

## Re-review of PR #223 at e883ae6

**Verdict: BLOCKING (2 items).** Last round's B1 is fixed. B2 is fixed only for crosses at 90 degrees: a skewed cross still reads a trusted wrong axis. There is also a new false refusal. Probes: about 360 fixtures, in a throwaway worktree, nothing committed.

### BLOCKING 1: a skewed cross still reads a trusted wrong axis, sometimes one that belongs to neither rod

The fixture is a single-band shaft r10 h100 along Z, crossed at the origin by a rod r10 h60 (or h100), tilted by `ang` about X. Every case below is `Ok`, `trusted = true`:

| ang | rod | axis read | aside |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5-40 deg | r10 h60, 1 or 5 bands | the **short rod's** axis exactly, e.g. 30 deg reads (0, -0.500, 0.866) | 0.056 |
| 5-45 deg | r10 h100, 1 band | **a line between the two rods**, e.g. 15 deg reads (0.004, -0.145, 0.990), 8.3 deg; 45 deg reads (-0.005, -0.279, 0.960), 16 deg | 0.086-0.088 |

The same fixture at 60 degrees is refused. With the Z shaft in 2 or 5 bands it reads Z, so the answer still depends on the band count.

Why it gets through: the single-band Z shaft's wall lines all pass through the origin, so they meet any line through it. Seen from an axis tilted by `ang`, those walls' bearings form a squashed ring, not a pile on 2 bearings. Their low moments are only about (1 - cos ang)/2, which is small. Weighted by area, that stays under `BIAS_SHARE`. A 90-degree cross gives the full k = 2 moment, which is why the perpendicular pins pass and the skewed ones don't. The "between the rods" axes come from `refine_dir` tilting freely inside the pencil: two pencils through one point meet every line through that point.

What this needs: the pencil test has to reject a pencil whose normals don't lie on a cone about the axis. A revolve's facets in one pencil share their angle to the axis. A ring about another axis seen obliquely does not: its angle to the axis varies with bearing. Example checks: the spread of `n . u` within each pencil, or comparing a pencil's moments against the ring it would make about its OWN best axis. Pin it with Z r10 h100 b1 crossed by r10 h60 at 30 degrees and by r10 h100 at 15 degrees: refused, or Z, never the tilted axis.

### BLOCKING 2 (regression): a square plate with a centred turned hole is now refused

`plate100 hole r20 t10`, `r40 t10` and `r45 t30` (two triangles per side face, a single-band bore, the top and bottom faces triangulated as an annulus) read Z exactly at 2fe41a2 and at 7fff05c. Now they are refused ("share no rotation axis", and "equally" for r45). The plate's side lines and the bore's lines meet at the same point, (0, 0, t/2), so they fall into one pencil. The plate's 4-bearing area is far over `BIAS_SHARE`. This undoes #204's stated gain (r45 t30 was "fixed by the PR"). Boring a centred hole in a square plate held in a 4-jaw chuck is ordinary lathe work, and Z through the bore is exactly right. Telling this apart from the cube-plus-boss case takes care, because both are a prism pencil plus a ring. The difference is that here the ring is itself a full ring about the axis, centred on the pencil point. Author's choice. At the least, this needs a deliberate decision in RECOMMENDED.md and a pin. Today nothing in the test suite covers it.

Also newly refused, which fails closed and is arguable, so not blocking:
- a 40x40x10 plate with a centred stem in 1 band (it read Z at 2fe41a2);
- a square (n4) flange on a single-band shaft (n6 and n8 flanges still read Z).

### What now holds (previous blockers and the requested hunts)
- **B1 fixed:** square bar 40 wide x 120-400 long with its sides split into 3/4/6/10, and a boss at (2.5,0), (5,0) or (10,10): all refused. The one-solid 3-step block, 3 stacked plates, 4 stacked cubes and the 2-step block with bosses in every position: all refused. Hex, octagonal and 12-sided prisms, plain or with sides split into 4, with a boss at (3,0) in 1 and 5 bands: refused.
- **Crosses at 90 degrees:** all 75 proportions (radii 10/10, 10/5 and 5/10; lengths 100/60, 60/60, 60/100, 200/40 and 40/200; bands 1/1, 1/5, 5/1, 5/5 and 2/2) read either the long or thick rod's axis, with the other rod set aside as a cross pin, or are refused. The short stub is never read.
- **Moment-test hunts:** stars of 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16 coplanar rods (r5 l60 and r3 l100, 1 and 5 bands), a 3-axis jack, a tilted tripod at 120 degrees, 4 and 8 rods arranged on a cone, a hub with 3 spokes at 120 degrees: all refused ("equally"). A hub with 3 through-rods (6 spokes) reads Z, the hub's own axis, which is correct.
- **Polygonal flanges** (n6 and n8, r40 t10 and r25 t20) on a shaft, with or without an off-centre boss: Z, exact.
- **Earlier set:** plates and cubes with off-centre bosses refused, the L-bracket and two diagonal cubes refused, and the round flange part exact (also tilted, also with a lug). Separate parallel bodies are refused; coaxial bodies read Z. T-junction meshes behave as before.

### False refusals of real turned parts
- Correct: cylinders in 1/2/3/5 bands; cones (r20->r5, r20->0, r5->r30, plus a 16-segment cone) in 1/2/5 bands; stepped and 3-step shafts; cross-hole shafts and the punched r10x40 bar (#116-like) in 1/2/5 bands; discs and short bars; shallow D-flats (depth 0.25, 0.5 and 1 in 1/2/3/5 bands, and a single-band D-flat with a cross hole at depth 0.5 and 1).
- Coarse cylinders: n16, n24 and n36 read Z. n6, n8 and n12 are refused. That is the sagitta skip budget (28.6 deg) that #204 already had, not this PR.

### Determinism, no panics, NaN
- Every fixture gave bit-identical results on a second run.
- A mesh with NaN, infinite, zero-area and 1e300 facets mixed in reads Z. An all-NaN mesh and a single triangle are refused by name. Cylinders at 1e8 and 1e-6 scale read Z.
- `unevenness` guards a zero or non-finite total, and the pencil peeling stops at `MAX_PENCILS`, below `MIN_PENCIL`, or on a pencil of fewer than 3 facets. No `unwrap` or `expect`.

Not approved, not merged.

Re-review blockers addressed in 1a42edf (plain push).

Each pencil is now judged by **latitude** (`n . u`, the angle at which a revolve's ring meets its axis). This replaces e883ae6's bearing-moment test.
- **Latitude classes.** The pencil's facets are sorted by latitude and split where it jumps by more than 0.01. Each narrow class (range at most 0.05) must hold a ring: its widest bearing skip must stay within twice the sagitta budget. Flats at a ring's latitude ride with it: a D-flat, a keyway floor confined to one band, and a square plate's sides round a centred bore (**B2**). A 90-degree cross folds the crossing wall onto two bearings at many latitudes, so none of those classes holds a ring.
- **Off-cone share (B1).** This is the share of the latitude's variance, and of its squared deviation, that the first two bearing harmonics explain (trigonometric regression of linear on circular data). A skewed ring seen from another axis swings its latitude once per turn, so it explains nearly all of it; a revolve's ring explains none. The share counts only once the explained swing passes 2e-3. The jittered-mesh pins reach at most 3.3e-4.
- **Cap.** The two are summed, weighted by area, and capped at 10 % of the inliers, as before. A drifted refined line through the shared point fails the same test, so it is rejected and the unrefined line stands.

New pins (both fail on e883ae6):
- `a_skewed_cross_never_reads_the_rod_or_a_line_between`: 5, 15, 30 and 45 degrees; rod r10 h60 and h100; 1 and 5 bands. Each case is refused or reads Z.
- `a_square_plate_with_a_centred_bore_reads_its_axis`: r20 t10, r40 t10 and r45 t30, all reading Z exactly.

Every earlier pin stays green, including the 90-degree crosses, the split and stacked prisms, the plate and cube with an off-centre boss, the single-band bar, the shallow D-flat, the keyed and noisy shafts, and the short bars.

Gate:
- motion lib: 145 tests passed.
- motion integration suites: multiaxis, multiaxis_avoid, multiaxis_rough, rotary, rotary_adaptive, rotary_links, rotary_offset and turning_* are green.
- app suites: drilling_cross*, lathe_* and turning* (21 binaries) are green.
- clippy on motion and app (all targets) is clean.

Decision and costs are recorded in RECOMMENDED.md. A skewed cross under about 0.1 degrees passes as one axis. A dome finer than 0.01 in latitude steps is judged by the off-cone share alone.

## Third review of PR #223 at 1a42edf

**Verdict: BLOCKING (1 item).** Round 2's two blockers are fixed. The latitude test leaves one hole: a finely meshed ball lets any set of flat faces through its centre "ride with a ring" about any axis. Probes: about 660 fixtures, in a throwaway worktree, nothing committed. Every one gave bit-identical results on a second run, nothing panicked, and the 30 `multiaxis::axis*` lib tests pass.

### BLOCKING: a fine ball plus flat faces through its centre reads a trusted axis across the flats

The fixtures are a UV sphere r30, plus a prism body centred on the sphere's centre (two bodies, as a multi-body STL exports them). Each reads `Ok`, `trusted = true`, aside 0.000:

| sphere mesh | second body | axis read |
|---|---|---|
| 120x60 (3-degree steps), 180x90, 360x180 | square rod 10x10x100 along **Z** | **X** or **Y** |
| same | square rod 6x6x80 along Z | X or Y |
| same | flat bar 40x4x100 along Z | Y |
| same, the whole part rotated and offset | square rod | the rotated cross axis |
| 72x36 | cube 50 | X (base read Z) |

Turning about X sweeps the 100 mm rod into a disc. The 72x36, 24x12 and 16x8 balls with a square rod are now refused. That is a gain: the base read X or Y for those too. So this hole is the base's, left open only for fine spheres, from about 3-degree facets upward, which is ordinary STL resolution.

The cause: the ball's facet lines all pass through its centre, so they join the same group as the prism's faces about any axis through it. The ball's latitudes about that axis run continuously with no jump over `LAT_GAP`, so the whole group is one class wider than `LAT_WIDE`, and `ringless` skips it. `off_cone` sees nothing: the rod's faces sit at latitude 0, or along the axis, at two bearings, and that pattern doesn't correlate with the first two harmonics of the bearing. Meanwhile the ball gives the coarseness gate every bearing. This is the "dome finer than 0.01 gets no ring check" cost, and its effect is a trusted wrong axis, not a refusal.

Suggested fix: inside a wide class, don't let coverage stand in for balance. Bin the class by latitude at `LAT_GAP` or so, and require each bin's area to spread across the bearings, for example the old area-weighted circular moments, applied per latitude bin. A sphere's equator bin is thin and even. A rod's faces dump many times that area onto 2 bearings in the same bin. Another way: take the flats (facets with a large area at one normal) out of a wide class and judge them as their own class. Pin it with a 120x60 ball plus a 10x10x100 square rod along Z: refused, or Z, never X or Y.

### Not blocking
- **The tiny-skew limit is larger than stated.** Two single-band r10 h100 rods crossing at 0.2 degrees read a trusted line at 0.22 degrees, and at 0.3 degrees they read 0.15 degrees. At 0.5 degrees the result is refused or Z. The worst offset is about 0.2 mm over the part, which is small. The PR text says "~0.1 degrees"; I'd update it to about 0.3 degrees.
- Newly refused, failing closed: a hex (n6) flange on a single-band shaft (n8 still reads Z, a square flange was already refused). Changed: a 72x36 ball plus a 50 mm cube reads X where the base read Z. Neither is turned stock.
- Already the same on the base, so not this PR: a fine torus (72x36, 36x12, 24x8) is refused as "equally", and a 16x6 torus reads Z. A cylinder-cone-cylinder with an r2 radial hole is refused.

### Round 2's blockers: fixed
- **Skewed crosses:** for 0.5-60 degrees, every rod size and band count (Z shaft in 1/2/5 bands, branch r10 h60, r10 h100 or r6 h60 in 1/5 bands) is refused or reads Z. The rod's axis is never read, and neither is a line between the rods.
- **Square plate with a centred bore** (r10, r20, r40 t10 and r45 t30): Z, exact.

### Still holding from earlier rounds
- Plates and cubes with off-centre bosses, the L-bracket and diagonal cubes: refused.
- Split square bars, stepped blocks, stacked blocks, and hex, octagonal and 12-sided prisms with bosses: refused. Irregular 16/20/24-gon prisms (alternating side lengths) read Z, also with an off-centre boss set aside. That's acceptable: Z is their centre.
- 90-degree crosses in all 75 proportions: the long or thick rod, or refused. Stars of 2-16 rods, a jack, a tripod, rods on a cone and a hub with 3 spokes: refused. A hub with 3 through-rods reads Z.
- Round, n6 and n8 flanges (with shafts in 5 bands) and the round flange part tilted and with a lug: exact.

### Domes, balls with flats, tori, cones meeting cylinders, coarse meshes
- A ball with two parallel flats (16x8 to 180x90) reads Z. A ball with one flat at x25 is refused at 72x36 and reads X at 180x90, which is correct: its flat's normal. Tilted, it reads the flat's normal.
- A dome (16x8 to 180x90) on a cylinder in 1 or 5 bands: Z. A dome on a square bar: refused.
- Cylinder-cone-cylinder (n16/24/72, 1/2/5 bands), a cylinder with a pointed cone, and near-cylinder tapers at latitude ~0.1 and ~0.01 (across the `LAT_GAP` split): Z, exact.
- Coarse cylinders and prisms: n14 and up read Z, with an off-centre boss set aside. n6/8/12 are refused by the sagitta budget, as on the base.

### False refusals of turned parts
None new among real revolves. All read exactly: cylinders in 1/2/3/5 bands; cones; stepped and 3-step shafts; cross-hole shafts; the #116-like punched bar in 1/2/5 bands; discs and short bars; tilted bars. Shallow D-flats (depth 0.25-1, any band count) read exactly, and so does a single-band keyway w3 d0.5. Deeper keyways and D-flats of depth 1.5 or more are refused, as on the base.

### Determinism, no panics, NaN
- `explained` returns 0 on a NaN or non-positive variance, and `ringless` uses checked slicing and `zip` (no indexing panics).
- A mesh with NaN, infinite, zero-area and 1e300 facets mixed in reads Z. An all-NaN mesh and a single triangle are refused by name. Cylinders at 1e8 and 1e-6 scale read Z.

Not approved, not merged.

Merging #204 and #223 back to back. Every wrong-axis family the three reviews found is fixed, and the remaining case (a fine ball plus a flat rod through its centre) also fails on main and on the base, so holding this back would leave more wrong axes live. That case is tracked as https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/237 (P0).
